title: The Software That Had to Remember Its Past
title_ja: 過去を覚える必要があったソフトウェア
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional software company develops a program that allows small organizations to create electronic records of their activities.
sentences.ja: 架空のソフトウェア会社が小組織の活動記録を作るプログラムを開発する。

sentences.en: The first version is relatively simple, and customers gradually accumulate large collections of information using the available features.
sentences.ja: 最初の版は比較的単純で顧客は機能を使って大量の情報を徐々に蓄積する。

sentences.en: Several years later, the developers propose changing the internal organization of the records in order to support functions that would be difficult to implement using the original design.
sentences.ja: 数年後、元設計では実装困難な機能を支えるため記録内部構造の変更を提案する。

sentences.en: The new program performs well when tested with information created after the change, and the developers are eager to release it to their customers.
sentences.ja: 変更後の情報で試すと新プログラムはよく機能し開発者は公開したがる。

sentences.en: A customer support employee nevertheless asks whether the program can correctly interpret records that were created before some of the current information categories existed.
sentences.ja: しかし現情報分類の一部が存在する前に作られた記録を正しく解釈できるか顧客支援職員が尋ねる。

sentences.en: The developers discover that an identical-looking entry may have been assigned different meanings in earlier versions of the program.
sentences.ja: 外見が同じ項目でも以前の版で違う意味を割り当てられていたと分かる。

sentences.en: A field that once contained a general description, for instance, might later have been divided into several more specific categories.
sentences.ja: 例えば以前一般説明を含んだ欄は後に複数のより具体的な分類に分かれたかもしれない。

sentences.en: Simply copying the old information into one of the new categories could therefore introduce assumptions that the person who originally created the entry had never intended to communicate.
sentences.ja: 旧情報を新分類の一つにコピーするだけで元の作成者が伝える意図のなかった前提を持ち込む可能性がある。

sentences.en: The team recognizes that transferring a record involves preserving its significance as well as retaining the characters or numbers stored by the earlier program.
sentences.ja: 記録移行には文字や数値を保持するだけでなく意味を保存することも伴うと認識する。

sentences.en: A successful conversion cannot be judged solely by comparing the amount of information present before and after the procedure.
sentences.ja: 変換成功は前後の情報量比較だけでは判断できない。

sentences.en: The company consequently develops a hypothetical conversion procedure that distinguishes records whose meaning is sufficiently clear from those requiring additional interpretation.
sentences.ja: そこで意味が十分明確な記録と追加解釈の必要な記録を区別する仮想変換手順を開発する。

sentences.en: Entries that cannot be classified confidently are displayed in a separate section rather than automatically assigned a category that might be inappropriate.
sentences.ja: 確信して分類できない項目は不適切かもしれない分類を自動付与せず別欄に表示する。

sentences.en: The developers also prepare explanations of the changes, so that customers can understand why an earlier record might appear differently after the transition.
sentences.ja: 以前の記録が移行後に違って見える理由を顧客が理解できるよう変更の説明も作る。

sentences.en: They consider whether preserving access to an original version of the information would help customers investigate unexpected discrepancies without requiring every organization to maintain an obsolete program indefinitely.
sentences.ja: 全組織に旧式プログラムの無期限維持を求めず元情報へのアクセスを残すことで予期しない食い違いの調査を助けられるか考える。

sentences.en: This proposal introduces additional technical responsibilities that must be examined in relation to the practical benefits it is expected to provide.
sentences.ja: この提案は期待利益に照らして調べるべき追加の技術的責任をもたらす。

sentences.en: Before introducing the new version, the company plans a series of fictional tests involving collections of records produced under different historical conditions rather than relying on examples created using the latest software alone.
sentences.ja: 新バージョン導入前に最新ソフトで作った例だけに頼らず異なる時期に作った記録集による架空試験を計画する。

sentences.en: The team identifies the information that should remain unchanged, the transformations that are intentional, and the situations in which a conversion must be reviewed.
sentences.ja: 変更しない情報、意図的な変換、確認が必要な状況を特定する。

sentences.en: The developers acknowledge that successful completion of these hypothetical exercises would not establish the security or reliability of any actual software system.
sentences.ja: 仮想活動の成功は実際のソフトウェアの安全性や信頼性を確定しないと認める。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the imagined case helps them articulate questions that a genuine evaluation would need to address before customers could responsibly depend on the revised program.
sentences.ja: それでも想像例は顧客が責任をもって修正版に頼る前に実評価が扱うべき問いを明確にする助けとなる。

sentences.en: The technical challenge concerns not only whether new functions operate as intended but also whether existing information remains understandable after the underlying arrangement has changed.
sentences.ja: 技術課題は新機能が意図通り動くかだけでなく基盤構造変化後も既存情報が理解可能かに関係する。

sentences.en: Software development often creates obligations toward people whose past decisions depended on the behavior of earlier versions of a product.
sentences.ja: ソフト開発は過去判断が以前の製品版の動作に依存した人々への義務を生むことが多い。

sentences.en: Improvements intended to make future activities easier can create unexpected difficulties when they alter assumptions on which existing records were based.
sentences.ja: 将来活動を容易にする改善も既存記録の前提を変えると予期しない困難を生み得る。

sentences.en: Responsible innovation therefore requires attention to the transition between different designs rather than comparing only their final capabilities in isolation.
sentences.ja: 責任ある革新には最終能力だけを切り離して比較せず設計間の移行への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: The fictional company discovers that an apparently outdated arrangement can contain information about the meaning of records that a more advanced program must still be capable of interpreting.
sentences.ja: 架空会社は一見時代遅れの構造も高度なプログラムがなお解釈できる必要のある記録の意味について情報を含むと知る。

sentences.en: Remembering the past is consequently part of building a system that people can continue using in the future.
sentences.ja: 過去を覚えておくことは人々が将来も使い続けられる仕組みの構築の一部である。

questions.prompt: Why do developers propose changing the internal design?
options: To prevent customers from creating records.
To support functions difficult to implement in the old structure.
To remove all earlier information.
To replace every customer.

questions.prompt: What limitation of initial testing is raised?
options: The program had never been tested on anything.
The new functions were all impossible.
Support employees cannot access software.
New records may not represent earlier record structures.

questions.prompt: How might an older field differ from later fields?
options: The older field necessarily contained no text.
Every later version has exactly the same meanings.
A general description may have been separated into specific categories.
All records were created on the same date.

questions.prompt: Why compare more than information quantity?
options: The meaning of information may change despite retaining its characters.
All copied information is automatically meaningless.
The number of records never matters.
Every conversion must remove information.

questions.prompt: What happens to entries that cannot be confidently classified?
options: They are automatically assigned a random category.
They are permanently deleted.
They are treated as newly created records.
They are displayed separately for further interpretation.
It ensures that no new feature is needed.
It could help investigate discrepancies after transition.
It makes every obsolete program permanently necessary.
It guarantees that all conversions are correct.

questions.prompt: Which tests does the team propose?
options: Tests using records produced under different historical conditions.
Tests using only the latest version's sample records.
Tests examining only the program's appearance.
Tests evaluating unrelated products.

questions.prompt: Why acknowledge the limits of the imagined tests?
options: No real evaluation could ever be useful.
The company has already proven every conversion safe.
A thought experiment cannot establish actual security or reliability.
The tests contain no relevant questions.
A new software feature.
Separation from other relevant things.
Repeated testing.
A successful conversion.
Responsible software changes must preserve the meaning of existing records through the transition.
New functions are the only measure of improvement.
All original software must remain unchanged forever.
Copying data guarantees that its meaning is preserved.

paraphrases.source: Simply copying the old information into one of the new categories could therefore introduce assumptions that the person who originally created the entry had never intended to communicate.

paraphrases.source: They consider whether preserving access to an original version of the information would help customers investigate unexpected discrepancies without requiring every organization to maintain an obsolete program indefinitely.

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 旧ソフト維持を強制しない。

paraphrases.rewrite: Responsible innovation evaluates the transition as well as the final designs.
